<!-- datagoodr research guide template.

     Customize without editing the package:
       - DG.R           custom functions & layout overrides
       - datagoodr.css  the page grid, fonts, and colors
     See vignette("customizing", package = "datagoodr").

     Render from the console with:  quarto::quarto_render("research-guide.qmd")
     or re-render against a different DGF/dataset without editing this file:
       datagoodr::update_rg("research-guide.qmd", DGF = "DGF-V2.xlsx") -->

<br>


<br><br>

```{r setup, echo=F, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# datagoodr is the only package this report needs to attach. Everything it
# renders is a datagoodr function, and those load what they need themselves.
library( datagoodr )

# Source the project customization file (custom functions / layout overrides)
# if it sits next to this document.
if( file.exists("DG.R") ) source("DG.R")


# The DGF drives the whole report. The path comes from the `dgf_file` param, so
# this document renders on its own - and update_rg() can point it at a
# different DGF at render time without editing this file.
dgf <- readxl::read_excel( params$dgf_file )

# Optional raw dataset. The report renders from the DGF alone - every statistic
# and graphic is already stored in its rg_* columns - so this stays NULL unless
# a caller supplies `data_file`. When supplied it is read once here and left
# available to DG.R and to any custom chunk that needs the underlying values.
raw.data <- if( is.null( params$data_file ) ) NULL else
            suppressMessages( readr::read_csv( params$data_file ) )


# Each variable type gets its own section because each plot type needs its own
# fig width and height. To add a new variable type:
# 1. add the new stable_data_type to the DGF
# 2. add a layout for it (see R/03-01-layouts.R)
# 3. add the functions that layout needs to read
# 4. add a dgf.TYPE subset and a section below

dgf.log  <-  dgf[ dgf$stable_data_type == "boolean",     ]
dgf.fact <-  dgf[ dgf$stable_data_type == "categorical", ]
dgf.chr  <-  dgf[ dgf$stable_data_type == "string",      ]
dgf.num  <-  dgf[ dgf$stable_data_type == "number",      ]


```


## Logical

```{r logical, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
create_all_sections( dgf.log )

```

## Factor

```{r factor, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
create_all_sections( dgf.fact )
```

## Numeric 

```{r numeric, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=2, echo=FALSE}
create_all_sections( dgf.num )
```

## Character

```{r character, results="asis", fig.width=8, fig.height=6, echo=FALSE}
create_all_sections( dgf.chr )
```




```{r datagoodr-style, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
# The report stylesheet comes from a single source: datagoodr.css (a local
# copy overrides the packaged one). Edit that file to restyle the report.
cat( "<style>\n", datagoodr_css(), "\n</style>\n" )
```

```{r datagoodr-record, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
# Provenance for this render - which DGF produced this file, its content hash,
# package/R/quarto versions, and when. Written as an HTML comment, so it travels
# with the report without appearing in it; read it back with
# datagoodr::read_render_record("research-guide.html").
#
#   visible  = TRUE  also prints it as a table in the report
#   identify = TRUE  adds your username and absolute paths. Off by default:
#                    this file is meant to be shared.
render_record( dgf, params$dgf_file, params$data_file )
```
